# Loop mode, loop counters and rotation

E2K has hardware support for counted and software-pipelined loops:

- a **loop status register** `%lsr` that counts iterations and splits a
  pipelined loop into prologue, kernel and epilogue;
- per-instruction controls: the `loop_mode` bit, `alc` (advance the
  loop counters), the `%LOOP_END` / `%NOT_LOOP_END` transfer conditions,
  and predicates derived from the counters (`%pcntN`, `%lcntex`);
- **rotating registers**: `abn` renames the based registers `%b[]` and
  `abp` the predicates `%pred0..psz`, so each iteration of an
  overlapped loop gets fresh registers under the same names.

A one-instruction loop-mode loop runs one iteration per cycle; the back
edge costs nothing. [apb.md](apb.md) builds on this (array prefetch is
correct only in a `loop_mode` loop counted by `%lsr`).

Status markers:

- **[hw]**: run on the Elbrus 4C (elbrus-v3) by
  `tools/isa-probes/loops.c` (cases generated by `gen_loops.py`), and
  for how soon register writes take effect by `lsrw.c` (`gen_lsrw.py`);
  `ldovl` by `isaleft.c` (`gen_isaleft.py`) and `apbst.c`
  (`gen_apbst.py`) on all three machines
- **[source]**: the kernel (`arch/e2k/include/asm/cpu_regs_types.h`
  `e2k_lsr_t`, `e2k_ilcr_t`), MCST's qemu (`target/e2k/tcg/translate-misc.c`
  `alc`, `translate-cds.c` stores and `%pcnt`, `translate-pls.c`
  `%lcntex`, `translate-mova.c`), gas (`tc-e2k.c`)
- **[guide]**: MCST programming guide 6.3 (software pipelining), 10.5
  (RLP/MRGC conditions), 10.11 (`abn`, `abp`, `abg`, `alc`)
- **[lcc]**: lcc 1.29.16 `-O3` output

## Registers [source, hw]

`%lsr` (loop status register, `rrd`/`rwd` number 0x83):

| Bits | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0–31 | `lcnt` | loop counter: iterations left in the kernel |
| 32–36 | `ecnt` | epilogue counter: extra iterations after `lcnt` runs out |
| 37 | `vlc` | the counter is valid; without it the loop never ends [hw] |
| 38 | `over` | set by the `alc` that ended the loop; read as `%lcntex` |
| 39 | `ldmc` | loads manual control: 1 keeps `mova` working in epilogue iterations [hw] |
| 40–47 | `ldovl` | load overlap: how many iterations ahead of a loop's movas the array prefetch unit may fetch; 0 behaves as no limit but the area's size; lcc writes 255 in small loops, 26–254 in many larger ones and 1–9 in loops that store into an array they stream (below, "Stores into a streamed array"). Only named in the kernel, gdb and the qemus, which don't implement it [source]; it changes no ordinary load, and `mova` results only through which stores the stream sees (below, "Array-prefetch depth") [hw] |
| 48–52 | `pcnt` | prologue counter |
| 53–59 | `strmd` | how many stores of the last iteration still write |
| 60 | `semc` | side effects manual control: no store suppression at all |

`%ilcr` (initial loop counters, 0x87) has `lcnt`, `ecnt` and `pcnt` at
the same places. **Writing `%lsr` also writes those fields of `%ilcr`**
[hw]; the loop doesn't change `%ilcr`, so `%ilcr − %lsr` is the number
of iterations done (the kernel uses this to restart array prefetch,
apb.md). v5+ add `%lsr1` (0xc3) and `%ilcr1` (0xc7): **`%lsr1` is the 64-bit
loop counter** [hw: Elbrus-8C2, `loops.c` built with `-DLOOPS_V5`].
Writing it sets the count: after `%lsr` with `lcnt` 5, writing `%lsr1`
= 7 makes the loop run 7 iterations and `%lsr` read back `lcnt` 7
(also 2, 1, 100; 0 behaves as `lcnt` 0 and runs once), and
`%lsr1` = 2³² + 3 runs exactly 4,294,967,299 iterations. Writing `%lsr`
**after** `%lsr1` resets `%lsr1` to the new `lcnt`, so write `%lsr`
first (control fields) and `%lsr1` second (the count), as lcc does
(`rwd %lsr` then `rwd n, %lsr1`). Each write also sets `%ilcr1` and
the `lcnt` field of `%ilcr` (the low 32 bits: after `%lsr1` = 2³² + 7,
`%ilcr` reads 7) [hw: `lsrw.c` `rb_lsr1_*`, 8C2, 2C3], and the loop
leaves both alone; `%lsr1` reads 0 after the loop. `ecnt`, `pcnt`
and the store rules work as with `%lsr` alone. The kernel saves `%lsr`, `%lsr1`, `%ilcr` and `%ilcr1` in a
signal context [source], and they are scratch across calls
([registers.md](../abi/registers.md)). User code may write `%ilcr`
too: no trap, `%lsr` unchanged, read back from 5 cycles (`ilcr_w`,
`rb_ilcr_ilcr_*`, all three machines); since the kernel's
array-prefetch restart reads it, nothing should.

**How soon writes take effect** [hw: `tools/isa-probes/lsrw.c`, three
runs on each of the 4C, 8C2 and 2C3 (v5 rows: 8C2, 2C3), 2026-10-12].
None of these is interlocked; the distance is in cycles from the
`rwd`:

| Write → reader | Old value at distance | New value from |
|---|---|---|
| `rwd %lsr` → `rrd %lsr` | 1–3 | 4 |
| `rwd %lsr` → `rrd %ilcr` | 1–4 | 5 |
| `rwd %ilcr` → `rrd %ilcr` | 1–4 | 5 |
| v5+: `rwd %lsr1` → `rrd %lsr1`, `rrd %lsr` (`lcnt`) | 1–3 | 4 |
| v5+: `rwd %lsr1` → `rrd %ilcr1`, `rrd %ilcr` | 1–4 | 5 |
| v5+: `rwd %lsr` → `rrd %lsr1` (the reset to `lcnt`) | 1–3 | 4 |
| `rwd %lsr` or `%lsr1` → the loop's `alc` and `%LOOP_END` | 1–3 | 4 |

For the loop this means: an iteration whose instruction issues 1–3
cycles after the write counts down the **old** `%lsr` and ends the loop
if the old value says so; from 4 cycles on the new count runs in full.
A one-instruction loop that should run 5 times (`lcnt` 5), entered D
cycles after the write, ran (every machine, every run unless noted
below):

| `%lsr` before the write | D = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4–6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vlc` 0 (`lsrw.c` finds 0x20ff0000000000 on entry: lcc's `%lsr` for a loop without a trip count, below) | 8 | 7 | 6 | 5 |
| `lcnt` 3 | 3 | 7 | 6 | 5 |
| `lcnt` 2 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 5 |
| `lcnt` 0, `ecnt` 2 | 3 | 7 | 6 | 5 |
| `lcnt` 1, or a finished loop | 1 | 1 | 1 | 5 |

That is 4 − D iterations of the old count and then the new count, or
only the old count's iterations if it ends the loop within those. A
`%lsr1` = 7 written D = 1, 2, 3, 4 cycles before the loop (`%lsr`
`lcnt` 5 long before) gave 10, 9, 8, 7, and so did lcc's order, `rwd
%lsr` and `rwd %lsr1` in consecutive instructions with the loop D
cycles after the second. Two writes apply in program order
even one cycle apart: `%lsr` then `%lsr1` counts `%lsr1` (7), `%lsr1`
then `%lsr` counts `%lsr`'s `lcnt` (5), with 1–5 cycles between them.
Of 510 loop counts in the three runs two differed, both on the 4C
(`lcnt` 2 at D = 1: 6; `lcnt` 3 at D = 1: 7), and each took 1–2 cycles
more than usual, as if the loop's first instruction had issued that
much later (inferred: the rule above at the later distance gives
exactly those counts); of 360 reads one saw the new `%ilcr` at
distance 1 (8C2), and a `rrd %lsr` 3 cycles after the write, right
after a loop that ended at once, read either value from run to run
(8C2, 2C3). In an earlier build of the probe two loops whose
instruction lay 0x40 bytes into a new page took 21–60 cycles for 5
iterations (4C every run, 2C3 once in three), consistent with a fetch
delay. That build also let gas's `CODE_PLACEMENT` padding (an empty
wide instruction before a jump target, [hwbugs.md](hwbugs.md)) add a
cycle before some loops, which made the counts look
placement-dependent; the probe now aligns its loop cases so that gas
pads none.

`loops.c`'s `early1`–`early3` (6, 6, 6 on all three machines) measure
distance 3 whatever their D: their `disp` comes 2 + D cycles before the
loop and a taken `ct` waits until 5 cycles after it
([control-transfer.md](control-transfer.md)), so their loop starts 3
cycles after the write and they show the `vlc` 0 row at D = 3. The
"one iteration too many" recorded here before, and the "one iteration"
once seen on the 2C3, are this rule after a `%lsr` with `vlc` 0 and
after a finished loop (inferred: the C code that runs before each case
decides which); v6 doesn't differ.

**Write `%lsr` and `%lsr1` at least 4 cycles before the loop's first
instruction** (and before any `rrd` of them); `%lsr` then `%lsr1` in
consecutive instructions is fine, as lcc does it.

## Instruction controls [source: bundle.md, gas]

| Control | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `loop_mode` | HS bit 10 (`lm`) | this instruction's stores obey the prologue/last-iteration rules below |
| `alc alcf=F, alct=T` | SS bits 16–17 | advance the counters if the instruction's transfer is not taken (F) / taken (T) |
| `abn abnf=F, abnt=T` | SS bits 21–22 | rotate `%b[]` likewise |
| `abp abpf=F, abpt=T` | SS bits 18–19 | rotate the predicates likewise |
| `abg N` (gas: a number, 2 = `abgi`, 1 = `abgd`) | SS bits 23–24 | rotate the global registers' based area (`%bgr`, below) |
| `ct ... ? %NOT_LOOP_END` (`%LOOP_END`, and combinations with a predicate) | ctcond types 4–7, 14, 15 | transfer on the loop-end condition |
| `op ? %pcntN` | RLP/MRGC condition (gas accepts it as `? %pcntN`) | true while `pcnt ≤ N` |
| `pass %lcntex, @pN` | ELP special predicate 0 | true when `over` is set |
| `setbn rsz, rbs, rcur` | CS1 | define the rotating area of `%b[]` |
| `setbp psz` | CS1 | rotate `%pred0..psz` |

## Semantics [hw]

**Counting.** Each `alc` (when its condition holds), using the values
before it:

- `%LOOP_END` = `vlc && lcnt < 2 && ecnt == 0`;
- `over` := `%LOOP_END`;
- `lcnt` decreases while above 1, then drops to 0; `pcnt` decreases
  while above 0; `ecnt` decreases once `lcnt < 2`.

So a loop `ct %ctpr1 ? %NOT_LOOP_END` with `alc` in the same instruction
runs **`lcnt + ecnt` iterations** (one when `lcnt` is 0 or 1); `pcnt`
doesn't add any:

| `lcnt`, `ecnt`, `pcnt` | Iterations | `%lsr` after |
|---|---|---|
| 5, 0, 0 | 5 | `lcnt` 0, `over` 1, `vlc` 1 |
| 1, 0, 0 / 0, 0, 0 | 1 / 1 | the same |
| 5, 2, 0 | 7 | `ecnt` 0 |
| 5, 0, 3 / 5, 2, 3 | 5 / 7 | `pcnt` 0 |
| `vlc` = 0 | never ends | |

**Predicates.** With `lcnt` 5, `ecnt` 2, `pcnt` 3 (`pcnt` 3, 2, 1, 0,
0, 0, 0 over the 7 iterations), an operation under `? %pcnt0` ran in 4
iterations and under `? %pcnt1` in 5: `%pcntN` is true when `pcnt ≤ N`
(true from the first iteration whose `pcnt` reaches N). `%lcntex` was
false in every iteration, epilogue included, and true after the loop:
it reads `over`, which only the final `alc` sets, so it tells code after
the loop that the counter ended it.

**Stores** in an instruction with `loop_mode` (when `semc` = 0):

- suppressed while `pcnt > 0` (prologue iterations);
- in the last iteration (`%LOOP_END`), the instruction's stores
  numbered `strmd` and up are suppressed (the first store in channel
  order is 0): `strmd` 0 drops them all, 1 keeps the first;
- `semc` = 1, or an instruction without `loop_mode`, stores in every
  iteration.

| `lcnt`, `ecnt`, `pcnt`, `strmd` | Iterations that stored (of 7, or 5) |
|---|---|
| 5, 0, 0, 0 | 1–4 (not the last) |
| 5, 2, 3, 0 | 4–6 |
| 5, 2, 3, 1 | 4–7; with two stores: the first in 4–7, the second in 4–6 |
| 5, 2, 3, 2 (two stores) | both in 4–7 |
| 5, 2, 3, `semc` = 1 | 1–7 |

A suppressed store doesn't reach the cache: `L1_QUERY` counts only the
stores that write (8 of 16 with `lcnt` 8, `pcnt` 3, `strmd` 0; 16 with
`pcnt` 0, `strmd` 2), and neither `COND_ALU_FALSE` nor `COND_AM_FALSE`
counts the others (`tools/isa-probes/pmu2.c` `c_lmst_*`, 4C, 8C2, 2C3;
[monitors.md](monitors.md)).

AAU stores (`staad … %aad0[ %aasti1 ]` with `incr`, as lcc pipelines
them) follow the same rules, and a suppressed one doesn't advance its
index either: with `pcnt` 3 the values of iterations 4, 5, 6 land in
elements 0, 1, 2 (and 7 in element 3 with `strmd` 1) [hw]. So a
pipelined loop's AAU stores need no address correction for the
prologue.

A **quad store counts as two stores** (v3 has only the AAU one in
64-bit mode, `staaq`; `stgdq` and `stapq` address through
protected-mode descriptors [source]): with `strmd` 0 the last iteration
drops it, with 2 it stores, and with 1, which would keep only its first
half, the `loop_mode` instruction raises SIGILL (`ILL_ILLOPC`) in that
iteration [hw]. A `strmd` count must therefore never split a quad
store. **On v5 a quad store is one store**: `stqp` (ALC2) and
`staaqp` (ALC5), one channel each, follow the rules with `strmd` 1
keeping the whole 16 bytes; with `stqp` in ALC2 and `std` in ALC5,
`strmd` 1 keeps the quad store and drops the doubleword (hw: Elbrus-8C2,
`v5qstores*`, `v5aaqstores`). Word stores (`staaw`) count
as one and advance by 4 bytes [hw].

**Loads are never suppressed**: an ordinary `ldd` in a `loop_mode`
instruction that reads past an array in epilogue iterations faults,
whatever `ldmc` (0, 1) and `ldovl` (0, 1, 2, 255) say. Loads that may
run past the data must be speculative (`ld,sm`, [speculation.md](speculation.md)),
as lcc's are.

**Array-prefetch reads** (`mova` in a `loop_mode` instruction) are
disabled in epilogue iterations unless `ldmc` = 1: with `lcnt` 5 and
`ecnt` 2, a `movad` of the stream 1, 2, 3, … returned 1–5 and then left
its destination unchanged (5, 5) with `ldmc` = 0, and continued (6, 7)
with `ldmc` = 1; `ldovl` 0, 1, 2 or 255 changed nothing [hw:
`tools/isa-probes/apb-loop.c`, `loopE`]. MCST's qemu has the same rule
(`mova` enabled when `!loop_mode || ldmc || !vlc || lcnt > 0`,
`translate-mova.c`) [source]. So epilogue iterations need no guard for
reads past the end of an array stream.

**Outside `loop_mode`** the `%lsr` state that disables a `mova` (`vlc`
1, `lcnt` 0, `ldmc` 0) changes nothing on the 4C and the 8C2: the
`mova` reads, in an epilogue iteration or after a loop has ended, as
MCST's qemu has it. On the 2C3 it is SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` instead
([hwbugs.md](hwbugs.md)) [hw: `tools/isa-probes/pocchk6.c` `seq`]. And
on v3–v5 the kernel adds epilogue iterations to a restarted stream's
position only when `ldmc` is set (`kernel/cpu/iset_v3.c:194-196`), so
an interrupt in an epilogue iteration without `ldmc` puts the stream
back: in 3,000,000 runs of such a loop (`De`: `lcnt` 62 + `ecnt` 2, no
`loop_mode`, one `movad` an iteration) 4–6 sums read one element twice,
on the 4C and on the 8C2, and none with `ldmc` 1 (`Dem`) or with `ecnt`
0 (`D`) [hw, two runs each]. So a `mova` that runs in an epilogue
iteration needs `ldmc` = 1, with or without `loop_mode`. lcc never
sets `ldmc`. Its loops with `ecnt` > 0 are common, and most of them
read through array prefetch ("How lcc builds loops"), but it puts every
`mova` in a `loop_mode` instruction, where the epilogue iterations
disable it (above) [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`; NPB LU class W on v3, v5.8c2 and
v6.2c3, BT and SP class A on v5.8c2 and v6.2c3: every `%lsr` it writes
has `ldmc` 0, and every wide instruction with a `mova` has `loop_mode`
(232, 287 and 288 in LU, 338 in BT, 546 in SP); e.g. v5 `blts`: `%lsr`
= 0xa6f72600000000 | n (`ecnt` 6), 35 movas].

**Array-prefetch depth (`ldovl`)** [hw: `tools/isa-probes/isaleft.c`
`ovst`, `ovs`, `ovtouch`; 4C, 8C2, 2C3]. `ldovl` limits how far ahead
of a `loop_mode` loop's movas the array prefetch unit fetches, in
iterations (in these loops each iteration advances its one area by one
element, so iterations and elements can't be told apart; the rows for
`ldovl` 1–8 are the same for every `asz`). It shows in two ways. A
64-iteration loop of 12 cycles reads `a[i]` with `movad` and stores
into `a[i + d]` (`ldmc` 0 and 1 alike, every run the same); the
smallest d whose stores the later movas see (distances 1, 2, 3, 4, 6,
8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 tried; "none": no store seen up to 48):

| `ldovl` | 4C | 8C2 | 2C3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 16 (at 12: 39 of 52) |
| 2 | 2 | 2 | 16 (at 12: 26 of 52) |
| 4 | 4 | 4 | 12 |
| 8 | 8 (at 6: 28 of 58) | 8 (at 6: 28 of 58) | 12 |
| 0 or 255, `asz` 0 (64 bytes, 8 elements) | 8 (at 6: 28 of 58) | 16 | 16 |
| 0 or 255, `asz` 2 (256 bytes) | 32 | none | none |
| 0 or 255, `asz` 5 (2 KiB) | none | none | none |

And from memory (best of 3, cycles per element, a 2 KiB area, one
`movad` an iteration): with a line an element the time falls as
1/`ldovl` until the area or the memory's bandwidth limits it, as if at
most `ldovl` fetches were in flight (inferred); consecutive doubles
share lines and fall more slowly:

| `ldovl` | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 255 | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4C, a 64-byte line an element | 96.5 | 48.5 | 24.6 | 12.6 | 6.6 | 3.7 | 3.2 | 3.6 | 3.4 | 3.6 |
| 8C2, the same | 193 | 96.2 | 50.0 | 25.7 | 13.1 | 7.4 | 4.6 | 4.4 | 4.1 | 4.2 |
| 2C3, the same | 336 | 193 | 96.4 | 22.7 | 11.6 | 5.8 | 2.9 | 2.7 | 2.7 | 2.7 |
| 4C, consecutive doubles | 27.0 | 18.8 | 14.1 | 12.5 | 6.2 | 3.2 | 1.63 | 1.11 | 1.09 | 1.06 |
| 8C2, the same | 44.0 | 32.9 | 27.0 | 24.4 | 12.4 | 6.4 | 3.32 | 1.87 | 1.22 | 1.05 |
| 2C3, the same | 93.7 | 56.2 | 51.3 | 48.9 | 24.2 | 5.8 | 2.95 | 1.46 | 1.10 | 1.06 |

A stream of 256 doubles that ends at the end of a touched page doesn't
touch the next, untouched page (no minor fault, `mincore` not
resident) for `asz` 0, 3 and 5 and `ldovl` 0 and 255, unless `ldmc` 1
and `ecnt` 8 make the movas themselves read there. So for a loop that
stores nothing into its streamed arrays a compiler writes 255, as lcc
does (0 was 3–16% faster than 255 for consecutive doubles in a
256-element area; for lines the two were within 7%, either way): a
small value throttles the stream.

**Stores into a streamed array** [hw: `tools/isa-probes/apbst.c`
(`gen_apbst.py`), 4C, 8C2, 2C3, 2026-10-16; lcc:
`tools/isa-probes/apbst-lcc.c`]. lcc 1.29.16 `-O3` does stream an array
that its loop stores into ahead of the reads, and limits the depth with
`ldovl`. For `a[i + d] = a[i] * 0.5 + 1` it uses plain loads for d 1–4
(and on v3, which streams none of these loops) and, from d = 5 on v5
and v6, an APB version with `ldovl` 1 (d 5–7) or 2 (d 8). For d 10 to
40 it streams 16 bytes an iteration (`movaqp`) with `ldovl` 1, 1, 2, 1,
1, 3, 4, 8 for d 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40 on v5, and the same on
v6 except 1, 5, 9 for d 24, 32, 40. In the scalar loops the store is
3 (d 5–7) or 4 (d 8) iterations ahead of the `mova` that reads its
element, and `ldovl` is 2 less (in the 16-byte loops 2 less up to d 24
on v5 and d 20 on v6, 3–4 less beyond). These loops compute right on
the 8C2 and on both cores of the 2C3 (25,600 checks each against a
reference that reads through a volatile). NPB's loops with array
prefetch write `ldovl` 26–255 (26 in SP's `lhsy` on v5, 27 on v6), why
is not checked; some loops without write 0, with `semc` set.

What a `mova` sees, by `apbst.c`: a 64-iteration loop reads a[i] with
`movad` from a 2 KiB area (`asz` 5, lcc's) and stores into a[i + d],
with `std` or with `staad` as lcc does (the same results but in the
one run named below), so the store is d iterations ahead of the `mova`
that reads its element. The table gives the smallest d from which
every later iteration saw the store, of the d tried (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8,
12, 16, 24, 32, 48), with partial counts in parentheses; "none": at no d tried (the
4C and 8C2 saw 1 of 32 at 32 and 1–2 of 16 at 48). Every case ran
twice with the same results, but one: on the 2C3 the waiting loop with
`%lsr1` and a base in `%aaind1` (`std_fast_a5_l1_ix`) at `ldovl` 2 saw
every store 4 iterations ahead in one run and none in its repeat and
in five later runs.

| Loop | `ldovl` 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 255 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4C, 8C2: waits for each `mova`'s result (8–12 cycles an iteration), store before the iteration's `alc` instruction | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 (at 6: 28 of 58) | none |
| 8C2: the same with the store in the `alc` instruction, where lcc puts it | 2 | 3 | 6 | 12 (at 8: 42 of 56) | none |
| 8C2: 2 or 5 cycles an iteration, `mova` results in rotating registers as in lcc's loops, the store in the `mova`'s instruction | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | none |
| 2C3: waits for each `mova` | 16 (at 12: 39 of 52) | 16 | 12 | 12 | none |
| 2C3: the same, writing `%lsr1` as lcc does | 12 | 12 | 8 | 8 | none |
| 2C3: `%lsr1`, store in the `alc` instruction | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | none |
| 2C3: 2 or 5 cycles an iteration | 4 (at 3: 42 of 57) | 4, or 6 at 5 cycles | 4 | 8 | none |

On the 4C and 8C2 a rule holds: with 1 ≤ `ldovl` ≤ d a `mova` sees a
store made d iterations earlier, and with the store in the iteration's
`alc` instruction it needs `ldovl` < d (shown at `ldovl` 1 and 2; at 4
and 8 the boundary lies in d 5 and 9–11, not tried). The 4C ran only
the loops that wait for their movas; the `alc` case and the fast loops
ran on the 8C2; v4 is not run, so "v3–v5" is an inference. `ldovl` 0
is no limit (the 2 KiB area saw no stores). lcc's scalar loops keep to
the rule with an iteration to spare. The cost is steep in fast loops:
the 2-cycle loop takes 1,456, 696, 380 and 280–320 cycles at `ldovl`
1, 2, 4 and 8 on the 8C2, against 196 at 255, and 504, 444, 504 and
288 on the 2C3, against 204. In loops that wait for their movas
`ldovl` 1 costs 1.3–2.3× on the 4C and 8C2 and nothing on the 2C3.

On all three machines the partial counts come in whole blocks: in each
32-byte block (four doubles; two-double halves in one 8C2 loop) the
first elements saw the store and the rest didn't (`apbst FILTER D`
prints which iterations saw it), as if the unit fetched a block at a
time (inferred). The 2C3 follows no `ldovl` rule. Which stores it sees
depends on the loop more than on `ldovl`: from 4–8 iterations ahead in
loops that don't wait for their movas, from 8 to 16 in loops that do.
Yet lcc's own v6 loops computed right with `ldovl` 1 and the store 3
iterations ahead (`ldovl` 2 and 4 ahead for d 8), in the `alc`
instruction, at 3–5 cycles an iteration, while the probe's 5-cycle
loop saw a store 3 iterations ahead only 3 times in 4. What lcc's loop
has that the probe lacks is not found: the store kind, `%lsr1`, an
index register (`%aaind1`) for the area, the store's place and the
loop's pace were each tried. So on v6 apb.md's rule stands: nothing
may store into an element that a later `mova` reads.

**Rotation.** `setbn rsz = R, rbs = B, rcur = C` makes `%b[]` a ring of
2(R + 1) 64-bit registers starting at window register 2B (`%b[n]` is
one 64-bit register, like `%dr`); `rcur` = C starts `%b[0]` C pairs up
the ring, at `%dr(2B + 2C)` (`rcur` 1, 2, 3 put `%b[0]` at `%dr18`,
`%dr20`, `%dr22` with B = 8). Each `abn` moves the base down one
register pair, so **the old `%b[0]` is the new `%b[2]`** (as
the guide's example says, 6.3.2): with `rsz` 3 (4 pairs from `%dr16`),
iterations writing `%b[0]` filled `%dr16`, `%dr22`, `%dr20`, `%dr18`,
`%dr16`, … `setbp psz = P` and `abp` do the same for `%pred0..P`: the
old `%pred0` is the new `%pred1`, the old `%predP` the new `%pred0`.
Reading through `%b[]` costs nothing beyond the operation's latency,
with 0 to 5 rotations between the write and the read (the most
measured): a pipelined daxpy's store bases read 0 to 5 rotations (3 to
21 cycles) after their `addd`, its load bases 0 to 5, and the same
values read through a fixed `%dr` all time the same
(`tools/isa-probes/stbase.c`, 4C, 8C2; timing.md, "Clusters").

**Early exits and while loops.** `ct %ctpr1 ? ~%pred0 &&
%NOT_LOOP_END` leaves when `%pred0` becomes true or the count runs out:
with `lcnt` 10 and the predicate true in iteration 4 the loop ran 4
times, with it never true 10 times. With `vlc` = 0 `%NOT_LOOP_END` is
always true, so the same loop is a plain while loop that only the
predicate ends (7 iterations), still with `alc`, rotation and the store
rules' prologue part (the last-iteration part needs `%LOOP_END`, which
never comes).

**Exits during the prologue.** In the combined conditions (ctcond types
6, 7, 14, 15: `[~]%predN || %LOOP_END`, `[~]%predN && %NOT_LOOP_END`)
the predicate is ignored while `pcnt` is not 0, unless `semc` is set:
with `pcnt` 1 or 3 and `vlc` 0, every type gives the loop condition
alone for both predicate values (`ct ? %pred0 && %NOT_LOOP_END` is
taken with `%pred0` false, `ct ? %pred0 || %LOOP_END` not taken with it
true), with or without `loop_mode`; with `pcnt` 0, or with `semc`,
they follow the predicate (`preds.c` `le_*`, outside a loop, 4C, 8C2,
2C3). So a pipelined while
loop's exit test can't act on a predicate its prologue stages haven't
computed yet ([predicates.md](predicates.md)).

**Calls.** A call doesn't touch `%lsr`: a loop calling a function that
leaves it alone counts right. A callee that runs its own loop leaves
`%lsr` finished (`lcnt` 0, `over` 1), and the caller's loop then ends
after the current iteration; saving `%lsr` with `rrd` before the call
and writing it back with `rwd` after (4 cycles before the next `alc`)
gives the right count. Restoring `%lsr` also resets `%ilcr`, which
matters only for array prefetch (apb.md).

**Interrupts.** 100,000,000 iterations of a loop whose rotating `%b[]`
chain counts them (each iteration writes `%b[2] + 1` to `%b[0]`) gave
the exact count and chain value with 10,965 `SIGALRM`s delivered during
the loop: the kernel saves and restores `%lsr`, `%ilcr` and the
rotation bases. A `loop_mode` store to a new page in each of 64
iterations page-faults every time and still stores every value, with
the right count.

**Timing.** A one-instruction `loop_mode` loop (`alc`, `ct ?
%NOT_LOOP_END`) runs 1,000 iterations in 1,001 cycles; with a second
instruction, 2,001: the transfer through a prepared `%ctpr1` is free
([control-transfer.md](control-transfer.md)).

## How lcc builds loops [lcc]

Counted loops (`for` with a known trip count):

In small loops that store into no array they stream, lcc writes
`%lsr` = `vlc` | `ldovl` 255 | `strmd` (0 if the loop stores nothing,
1 or 2 in the loops probed) | `lcnt` = n (`addd 0x20ff2000000000`,
`insfd` of n), at least 4 cycles before the loop, and uses no `pcnt` or
`ecnt`: it **peels the prologue** (the first stages run before the
loop, with `,sm` operations) and leaves the epilogue to the
last-iteration store rule and speculative loads. A small loop that
does store into a streamed array gets `ldovl` 1–9 and, in its 16-byte
versions, `pcnt` = `ecnt` 2–8 (`apbst-lcc.c`; "Stores into a streamed
array", above). Larger loops often use `pcnt` and `ecnt`, always
equal, and most write `ldovl` below 255. In NPB at `-O3`, of the
loop-mode loops 56–63 of LU's 96 have `ecnt` > 0 (v3, v5, v6; 9–11
more compute `%lsr` at run time), 33 of BT's 63 on v5 and 31 of 64 on
v6, and 133 of SP's 312 on v5 but 39 on v6; nearly all of these read
through array prefetch. `buts`'s first loop writes `%lsr` =
0xa2ff2200000000 | n (`ecnt` 2, `pcnt` 2, `strmd` 5) on v3, v5 and v6,
the v3 code's rotating loops in `buts` and `blts` 0xa8ff2800000000 | n
(`ecnt` 8, `pcnt` 8, `strmd` 5), and v5's `blts` 0xa6f72600000000 | n
(`ecnt` 6, `ldovl` 247); their DAM lock loads (`mas=0x4,sm`) and check
loads (`mas=0x3`) run under `? %pcnt0` and higher [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`;
NPB LU class W, BT and SP class A]. The kernel is one
instruction or a few, each with `loop_mode`, the last with `alc`, `abn`
(and `abp` when predicates rotate) and `ct %ctpr1 ? %NOT_LOOP_END`, the
CTPR prepared before the loop. Rotating `%b[]` carry values between
stages (`setbn rsz = 3..8` in the small kernels probed, up to 0x3b in
NPB LU's `rhs`, below); stores often go through the array
prefetch unit (`staad … %aad0[ %aasti1 ]` with `incr`). Example,
`a[i] = b[i] * s` with `restrict`:

```
.L7: { loop_mode; alc alcf=1, alct=1; abn abnf=1, abnt=1
       ct %ctpr1 ? %NOT_LOOP_END
       fmuld,0,sm %b[7], %r2, %b[0]
       addd,1,sm 0x8, %b[11], %b[9]
       ldd,2,sm %r1, %b[11], %b[1]
       staad,5 %b[12], %aad0[ %aasti1 ]; incr,5 %aaincr0 }
```

The peeled prologue is list-scheduled, not run as copies of the
kernel: in NPB CG's row loop (`sum += a[k] * p[colidx[k]]`, kernel II
4, `colidx` and `a` through array prefetch on v5 and v6, plain loads on
v3) lcc uses the gathered `p[colidx[k]]` 13 iterations after loading it
on v5 and v6 and 8 on v3, and issues the first 14 iterations' loads
(45, up to four a wide instruction) in 23 wide instructions, 27 cycles,
before the kernel (v5; v6: 47 loads in 22) [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, NPB CG
class W].

Big counted loops are not overlapped: NPB LU's `jacld`, `jacu` and
`blts` are one-stage `loop_mode` kernels, `alc` and `ct %ctpr1 ?
%NOT_LOOP_END` with no `abn`, the count only in `%lsr` (written in the
preheader) [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, NPB LU class W; cycles are the wide
instructions plus their `nop` cycles]:

| Loop | v3 (`e2k-v3.4c`) | v5 (`e2k-v5.8c2`) and v6 (`e2k-v6.2c3`) |
|---|---|---|
| `jacld`, `jacu` | 116 wide instructions, 118 cycles; 467 operations, 20 `movad` | 105–106 wide instructions, 106 cycles; 465 operations, 20 `movad` |
| `blts` | 129 wide instructions, 239 cycles; 341 operations, 94 plain loads | 112 wide instructions, 253 cycles; 322 operations, 85 `movad` |

`jacld` stores 100 elements an iteration (75 `staad`, 25 `std`, all in
ALC2 and ALC5) with no frame access in the kernel, re-reads all 20 `u` elements it
needs through array prefetch rather than carrying the previous
iteration's, and names 177 distinct registers in the v5 kernel (98
`%b[]` under `setwd wsz = 0x60; setbn rsz = 0x3f, rbs = 0x20`, 63 `%r`,
`%g16`–`%g31`); it stores 29 of its 34 constant zeros in its first 52
wide instructions and 51 of its 66 computed values in its last 26, two
a cycle. `blts` carries `v[i][j-1][k][0..4]` in registers; 5 of its 9
`fdivd` are on that recurrence, which bounds its operations to 209
cycles an iteration on all three versions (isa-score's `score.py`).

Around these loops lcc keeps the function's own layout and puts what
crosses a loop out of the loop's way [lcc 1.29.16 `-O3`, NPB LU class W,
v3, v5, v6]:

- The one-stage kernels (those above and `buts`'s main loop, 320–470
  operations; `buts`'s first loop, about 160 operations in 61–65 wide
  instructions, rotates) name `%b[]` like `%r`. `jacld` and `jacu` go up
  to `%b[127]` under the function's `setbn rsz = 0x3f, rbs = 0x20, rcur
  = 0`, set at entry. A value of the enclosing loop stays in a register
  the kernel doesn't write (`%r3`–`%r5` are read inside as invariants).
  On v5 and v6, where the kernel names 177 registers, `jacld` and
  `jacu` store three such values to the frame before the loop (`,sm`
  stores) and fill them after it (`mas = 0x4`). In `jacld` these are
  the bound `iend`, the argument `k`, and a zero for an AAU descriptor.
  v3's kernels name 172–173 registers (`jacld` 173, `jacu` 172) and
  spill nothing.
- `rhs` (`wsz = 0x60`, `setbn rsz = 0x3f, rbs = 0x20` between its
  loops) has 31 small loops that rotate. Each is 3–11 wide instructions
  with `abn`, under its own `setbn rbs = 0x20, rcur = 0`, with `rsz`
  0xc–0x34 on v3, 0x26–0x3b on v5 and 0x1b–0x3b on v6. They name up to
  `%b[119]` and read their invariants from 1–7 `%r`. A value that lives
  across such a loop is in `%r` or in a `%b[k]` above that loop's ring
  (k ≥ 2(`rsz` + 1)), never in the ring: `%b[97..127]` on v3 and
  `%b[107..127]` on v5 and v6, across 27–30 of the 31 loops on v3,
  15–17 on v5 and 11–13 on v6 (the ranges between a path-by-path
  liveness bound and a straight-line one), the lowest of them at least
  9 registers above the ring. After the loop's closing `setbn rsz =
  0x3f`, `%b[k]` names the same `%dr(64 + k)` again. In `buts` and
  `blts` the same holds: on v5 and v6 `buts`'s crossing values sit above
  its rings, and on v3 (and in v5 and v6 `blts`) the function's own
  `%b` area lies inside the ring, so values crossing it are only in
  `%r`.
- MCST's qemu treats a `%b[k]` above the ring as out of reach inside
  such a loop: it raises the window-bounds exception for
  k ≥ 2(`rsz` + 1) (`OpenE2K/qemu-e2k-mcst/target/e2k/reg-index.h:40`)
  [source], and gdb shows it as `<unavailable>` ([registers.md](../abi/registers.md),
  "How MCST's gdb reads them"); the hardware is not checked ("Not
  checked yet"). lcc's loops never name one.

Loops without a trip count (`while`, early exits): `%lsr` without `vlc`
(`0x20ff0000000000`: `ldovl` 255, `strmd` 1), the same `loop_mode`,
`alc`, `abn` and `abp`, and an exit through a rotated predicate
(`ct %ctpr1 ? %pred1`) or `ct %ctpr1 ? ~%pred0 && %NOT_LOOP_END`. In
these, lcc also conditions prologue work on `%pcntN`: in CoreMark's
`matrix_test` a DAM lock load runs under `? %pcnt14` and its check
under `? %pcnt0`. Over CoreMark and Linpack at `-O3`/`-O4` lcc uses
`%pcnt0` … `%pcnt14` and `rcur` up to 0x24, never `abg`, `%lcntex` or a
read of `%lsr`, and never a call inside a loop-mode loop.

## For a compiler

- A counted loop needs no compare: `rwd` the count into `%lsr` (with
  `vlc`) at least 4 cycles ahead, `disp %ctpr1, head` 5 cycles ahead,
  and end the body with `alc` and `ct %ctpr1 ? %NOT_LOOP_END` (GCC's
  `doloop_end`; port plan 7.7). An `ibranch` back edge would cost 6
  cycles per iteration.
- In a pipelined loop give every store `loop_mode` and either peel the
  prologue (lcc) or set `pcnt` to the number of prologue stages; set
  `strmd` to the number of stores of the final stage that must still
  write in the last iteration; make every load that can run ahead
  speculative.
- Values that live across stages go in `%b[]`; a value produced in
  stage s and used k iterations later is named `%b[n + 2k]` at the use.
- **Schedule with the crossing cost** (timing.md) on every dependence
  whose producer and consumer may land in different clusters, which is
  any dependence when gas picks the channels: a one-instruction kernel
  that carries an integer value to the next iteration at exactly its
  latency runs 1,000 iterations in 1,001 cycles with the consumer in the
  producer's cluster but 4,989 with it in the other one (a 4-cycle stall
  every iteration), and 1,001 again when the use waits one more
  iteration (`rot_*` cases, 4C and Elbrus-8C2 alike). Padding only adds
  stages; an operation's use of its own previous result stays in one
  channel and needs no padding. (Proof-of-concept back end: daxpy at
  II 1 ran at about 5 cycles per element with plain latencies, 0.75 ns
  with crossings added, lcc 0.70.)
- **No `loop_mode` is needed** if the kernel's stores all sit in its
  last stage and every other operation is speculative: with `lcnt` = n
  (and `vlc`, no `pcnt`, `ecnt` or `strmd`) the kernel runs n times;
  iteration k runs stage s of source iteration k + S − 1 − s, so the
  last S − 1 kernel iterations only run early stages of iterations past
  the end, whose loads are speculative and whose results nothing
  stores. The peeled prologue runs stages 0..S−2 of iterations 0..S−2
  under the names those values have after the skipped rotations.
  `abn abnf=1` also rotates on the iteration that leaves the loop, so
  afterwards the last iteration's value written as `%b[X]` is
  `%b[X + 2]` (`rot_exit`, 4C and 8C2), and one defined in stage D is
  `%b[X + 2 (S − D)]`. (Proof-of-concept back end, 4C and 8C2: sums,
  dot products, scaling, copies and daxpy for n = 1..1023, including
  n below the stage count and overlapping arrays.)
- **In a function that calls**, the ring must not stay above the
  outgoing pairs at a call: the callee would inherit the ring with them
  (`wsz − wbs` pairs, registers.md), and the PLT stub's `setwd wsz = 8`
  traps with SIGILL `ILL_ILLOPC` (proof-of-concept back end, 4C). lcc
  keeps the window at locals + 4 outgoing pairs (`setbn rsz = 3, rbs`
  at the outgoing pairs, calls with that `wbs`), and around the loop
  **grows the window** with a second `setwd` and a ring starting at the
  outgoing pairs (`setwd wsz = 0x1d; setbn rsz = 0xf, rbs = 0xd`), then
  shrinks it back after the loop (`setwd wsz = 0x11; setbn rsz = 0x3,
  rbs = 0xd, rcur = 0`) [lcc]. The proof-of-concept back end instead
  puts the ring between the locals and the outgoing pairs (calls with
  `wbs` above it, `setbn rsz = 3` at the outgoing pairs after the loop),
  which also works on the 4C and keeps the diagnostic values the last
  kernel iterations leave in the ring out of the argument registers.
- A loop with a call (lcc never pipelines one, guide 6.3.3) must save
  `%lsr` around it unless the callee is known not to run a loop:
  calls don't preserve it, they just don't change it.
- A loop without a known trip count can still use loop mode: `%lsr`
  without `vlc`, and an exit predicate in the back edge's condition.

## Emulators

| | 4C | MCST's qemu | Community qemu |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rrd %ilcr` | the counters | aborts ("%undef", unimplemented) | works |
| `rwd %lsr` sets `%ilcr` | yes | no (TODO in `translate-al-c14.c`) | yes |
| `%lcntex` inside the loop | false | (not run) | true in epilogue iterations |
| `semc` = 1 | stores in every iteration | (not run) | still suppresses prologue stores |
| loop entered 1–3 cycles after `rwd %lsr` | one extra iteration | (not run) | right count |

The rest of `loops.c` matches the 4C under the community qemu.

## Global register rotation (`abg`, `%bgr`) [hw: Elbrus-8C2 and 4C, source]

Run on the Elbrus-8C2 (v5) and the 4C (v3) by `tools/isa-probes/abg.c`
(one case per process). Everything below holds on both.

`%bgr` (11 bits): `val` (bits 0–7) marks which of the eight physical
rotating registers are valid, `cur` (bits 8–10) is the rotation offset.
Processes start with `%bgr` = 0x0ff (`cur` 0, all valid), and user code
can read and write it with `rrs`/`rws`. `%g24`–`%g31` name physical
global `24 + ((cur + n) & 7)`; `%g0`–`%g23` don't rotate. Each 64-bit
half of a quad access (`movtq %qg24`, v5 `qpand %qpg24`) rotates on its
own, also with an odd `cur`.

It is an x87-style register stack (presumably for MCST's x86 binary
translator), `cur` being the top:

| Operation | Effect | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| `abg 1` (`abgd`, push) | `cur` −= 1 (mod 8), then set `val` bit `cur` | SIGFPE `FPE_FLTINV` if that bit was already set (overflow) |
| `abg 2` (`abgi`, pop) | clear `val` bit `cur`, then `cur` += 1 | never, even if the bit was clear |
| `abg 3` | as `abg 1` | as `abg 1` |
| read of `%g24`–`%g31` in ALC4/ALC5 | the value | SIGFPE `FPE_FLTINV` if the physical register's `val` bit is clear (`exc_fp_stack_u`) |
| the same read with `,sm`, or in ALC0–ALC3 | the value, not diagnostic | never |
| write of `%g24`–`%g31` | the value | never; `val` doesn't change |

The kernel's trap entry saves `%bgr` and sets it to 0x0ff before
touching `%g24`–`%g31` (MCST's 6.1-1.17 and later; the 4C's 6.1-1.9
saves the globals first), restores it on return, and starts signal
handlers with 0x0ff (`trap_table.S.h`, `signal.c`); a trap taken with
invalid slots is harmless on both machines. But on the 4C a kernel
entry under a nonzero `cur` can move the values of `%g24`–`%g31`
(after a signal, `%g(24 + n)` held the old `%g(24 + ((n − cur) & 7))`;
[kernel-interface.md](../abi/kernel-interface.md), "The rotating
globals in the frame").

Delays (`tools/isa-probes/native.c`, 4C and 8C2): after `abgd` or
`abgi` the next wide instruction already names the registers by the
new `cur` (a read in the same instruction sees the old naming); after
`rws %bgr` a read sees the new naming from 10 cycles on, or in the next
instruction after a `wait all_e`.

lcc never emits `abg` or touches `%bgr`, so a compiler can ignore them;
the ABI treats `%g24`–`%g31` as scratch (spec/abi/registers.md). v6
replaces `abg` with `abgc`/`rbgc` (bundle.md). Neither emulator runs
this: MCST's qemu stops at `rrs %bgr` ("exception handling is
unimplemented") and decodes `abg` without executing it; the community
qemu gives SIGILL.

## v6 [hw: Elbrus-2C3]

`loops.c` (with the v5 cases) and `lsrw.c` give the 8C2's results on
the 2C3: write timing ("Registers"), counts, `%pcnt`/`%lcntex`, store
suppression, rotation, `%lsr1`, quad stores and the behaviour across
signals and page faults are the same.

gas rejects `abg` for v6 ("not supported on elbrus-v6"), so `abg.c`
doesn't build there. v6 splits the x87-style stack into plain moves and
separate checks (`ctl6.c`, from user mode; `cur` is `%bgr` bits 8–10,
`val` bits 0–7, and a mask is rotated left by `cur`, so bit 0 means the
current top):

| Operation | Effect |
|---|---|
| `abgc N [? %predN]` (N 1–7, SS) | `cur` += N (mod 8); `val` unchanged, never traps (v5's `abgd`/`abgi` check `val` and trap) |
| `rbgc [? %predN]` | `cur` = 0; `val` unchanged |
| `modbgv a, dst` (ALC1/4) | `val` = (`val` & ~rot(a[7:0])) \| rot(a[15:8]): marks registers empty or full; writes 0 |
| `vfbgv a, b, dst` | SIGFPE `FPE_FLTINV` (an x87 stack fault) if a register in rot(b[7:0]) is full (overflow) or one in rot(b[15:8]) is empty (underflow); else writes 0 |
| `mkfsw a, b, dst` | the x87 status word with TOP = b mod 8 (semantics.md, "v6 operations") |

`abgc` and `rbgc` take effect for the next wide instruction: `rrs %bgr`
or `vfbgv` in their own instruction sees the old `cur`, one instruction
later the new one, and nothing stalls (a block of `abgc 1` + `rrs %bgr`,
`abgc 1` + `vfbgv` or `abgc 1` + a read of `%dg24` takes one cycle per
instruction, as with a `nop` in place of `abgc`) [hw: `ctlleft.c`
`abgc_*`, `rbgc_*`, `t6_abgc*`, 2C3]. (On v3–v5 `abgd`/`abgi` also act
on the next instruction, while `rws %bgr` needs 10 cycles; above.)

**v6 doesn't rename the rotating globals any more**: after `abgc 1`, or
`rws` of `%bgr` with `cur` 1, `%bgr` reads `cur` 1 but `%g24` still
names physical register 24 (`%g25` 25), at any distance and after `wait
all_e` (`native.c` on the 2C3). `cur` is bookkeeping for the x87 helpers
only. A C compiler still has no use for them.

## Not checked yet

(v7 is out of scope: not in silicon.)

- What the hardware does with a `%b[k]` beyond the ring (k ≥
  2(`rsz` + 1)): MCST's qemu raises the window-bounds exception, and
  lcc's loops never name one ("How lcc builds loops").
- Which stores a 2C3 `mova` sees ("Stores into a streamed array"): why
  lcc's v6 loops with a store 3 iterations ahead at `ldovl` 1 compute
  right when the probe's loops miss such stores; and on the 4C and
  8C2, the rule's boundary at `ldovl` 4 and 8 with the store in the
  `alc` instruction (d 5, 9–11), and the 4C's fast loops.
- How lcc picks the `ldovl` of NPB's loops (26–254).
